# Release check — v1.3.0, 2026-09-24

The manual pass required by README's "Before publishing" and by
`scripts/prepublish-check.js`. Performed by Claude against pages built from
**this branch's** scaffolds — not pages generated by an earlier version — and
this repository's own map: 65 files, 695 functions, 8 of 8 entry points traced.

v1.3.0 added `qa.template.html` as a fifth scaffold and two commands, so the
checklist grew from four pages and three skills to five pages and four skills.
The last pass ([RELEASE-CHECK-2026-08-28.md](RELEASE-CHECK-2026-08-28.md)) does
not cover either new page, which is why this one exists rather than a note
saying the previous one still stands.

Pages were built by filling each shipped scaffold's tokens the way the prompt
prose instructs, then served over `http://127.0.0.1:4319` and opened in headless
Chromium. Every number below was read out of the live document, not out of the
source that produced it.

**Step 4 was performed by the maintainer, on their own project, outside this
environment — see "Step 4" at the end. Claude did not observe it.**

## What produced the data

Three scripts, all in the session scratchpad rather than in the repository,
because each is the mechanical half of a prompt and none of them is a product:

- `scripts/build-map.py` (which *is* in the repository) ran the five tracers over
  this repository and merged them into `Code_Flows/`.
- A detector script implemented the ten quality detectors whose thresholds are
  written as numbers in `templates/claude/code-flow.quality.md`, over that map.
  Step 4b — verifying a candidate against source — was done by hand, by reading:
  five findings were read and marked `verified`, and one was read, contradicted
  and **dropped**, which the report's coverage banner reports as
  `1 finding dropped as stale`.
- A QA script implemented the five static checks `/code-flow.qa` describes —
  `entry-exists`, `node-resolves`, `edge-holds`, `reachable`, `current` — against
  the map and the current source.

The violations document's two findings were settled by reading the files they
cite. Both are real, and both are fixed here (see "What this pass found") — the
report was generated before the fix, which is why it still shows them.

## Step 1 — every page renders

| Page | Scaffold | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `index.html` | `index.template.html` | Renders. Title `code-flow-skill · code flow`, heading `8 mapped flows`, 8 flow cards linking to 8 flow pages plus the quality report |
| `templates_shared_tracers_trace_python_main.html` | `viewer.template.html` | Renders. 42 graph nodes, 202 SVG paths, chips `entry 1` / `step 41` |
| `templates_shared_tracers_trace_typescript_trace.html` | `viewer.template.html` | Renders. 64 nodes, 338 paths |
| `quality-report.html` | `report.template.html` | Renders. Coverage reads "8 of 8 entry points found were traced", 47 findings, chips across DRY, KISS and YAGNI |
| `violations-report.html` | `report.template.html`, `meta.kind: "violations"` | Renders. Heading reads **Code Flow — Violations**, 2 findings, chips `RULES` / `rule-violation` |
| `qa-report.html` | `qa.template.html` | Renders. Verdict "Nothing is broken. 16 of 16 checked things passed every check that ran", 16 subject cards, 72 checks |
| `qa-drift.html` | `qa.template.html` | Renders. All four statuses on one page: 1 broken, 4 drifted, 1 unchecked, 10 pass |
| `code-flow.html` | `bundle.template.html` | Renders all three in one document — see below |

**No page errors on any of them.** `pageerror`, `console.error` and
`requestfailed` were all listened for; every page reported none. The one console
404 the v1.2.0 pass saw on `index.html` did not recur, and the page's outbound
references were enumerated to confirm why: 25 `href`s, every one of them a
sibling `.html`, `.md` or `.json` artifact, and not a single `src=` or
`<link>`. The page requests nothing.

Three things v1.3.0 changed were confirmed in the rendered page rather than in
the template source:

- **The violations page does not borrow the quality page's reassurance.** Its
  banner carries `4 source files read` — a fact `report.template.html` prints
  only when `meta.kind` is `violations` — and it does **not** carry the
  "No detectors were skipped" line or name the twelve quality detectors as having
  run clean. The quality page, from the same scaffold, carries both.
- **QA's four statuses are distinguishable.** `qa-drift.html` draws `broken`,
  `drifted`, `unchecked` and `pass` chips, ordered broken-first, each subject
  card carrying the named checks that produced its status.
- **A pass still has to say what held.** The scaffold's validator refuses a
  `pass` with an empty `checks` array; every one of the 16 passing subjects
  carries between 4 and 5 named checks.

**Arrowheads.** Every edge group in a diagram carries its own arrowhead element
— 49 of 49 on the Python flow, 83 of 83 on the TypeScript flow — drawn as a
`path.ah` sibling of the edge line. Confirmed visually in a screenshot as well
as by counting.

**No fragment-id references survive.** Across all eight pages: 0 `<marker>`
elements, 0 `marker-end`/`marker-start` attributes and 0 `url(#` occurrences in
the whole serialized DOM. That is what keeps a generated page out of a corporate
mail gateway's quarantine.

**The bundle does all three in one document.** Its landing view lists the same 8
flows as `index.html`; opening the first gives
`#/flow/templates_shared_tracers_trace_c_family_main` with **78 nodes**, the same
number the standalone page for that flow draws; `#/report` reaches **47
findings**, the same number `quality-report.html` shows. No page errors.

## Step 2 — corrupted data shows the error card, not a blank page

The opening `{` was deleted from each page's embedded JSON block. Each result was
confirmed unparseable by `json.loads` **before** loading, so the check cannot
pass vacuously — the v1.1.0 pass threw out a first attempt that had corrupted a
character inside a string, which leaves JSON valid.

| Page | Block | Shown | Page still drawn |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index.html` | `#index-data` | `Invalid JSON in #index-data` + parser message + the `<\/` tip | 18,653 chars |
| `templates_shared_tracers_trace_python_main.html` | `#flow-data` | `Invalid JSON in #flow-data` + message + tip | 95,159 chars |
| `quality-report.html` | `#report-data` | `Invalid JSON in #report-data` + message + tip | 73,389 chars |
| `violations-report.html` | `#report-data` | `Invalid JSON in #report-data` + message + tip | 27,945 chars |
| `qa-report.html` | `#qa-data` | `Invalid JSON in #qa-data` + message + tip | 29,180 chars |
| `code-flow.html` | `#bundle-data` | `Bundle failed to load — Invalid JSON in bundle data:` + message | 506,534 chars |

No uncaught exception on any of the six. No page was blank.

## Step 5 — a user theme applies in both modes

`--accent` was **uncommented in both blocks** of a copy of the shipped
`theme.css`, with a different value per block, exactly as a user edits
`.code-flow/theme.css`:

```css
:root{ --accent:#ff2d95; }
[data-theme="light"]{ --accent:#008b45; }
```

Read from the live document, and compared against the same page built from the
stock theme so the check shows a pixel changing rather than a variable resolving:

| Page | Theme | Mode | `.coverage-banner h2` computed colour | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `quality-report.html` | stock | dark | `rgb(145, 132, 217)` | built-in |
| `quality-report.html` | stock | light | `rgb(93, 82, 148)` | built-in |
| `quality-report.html` | user | dark | `rgb(255, 45, 149)` | `#ff2d95` ✓ |
| `quality-report.html` | user | light | `rgb(0, 139, 69)` | `#008b45` ✓ |
| `qa-report.html` | user | dark | `rgb(255, 45, 149)` | `#ff2d95` ✓ |
| `qa-report.html` | user | light | `rgb(0, 139, 69)` | `#008b45` ✓ |

`qa.template.html` inlines the theme the same way the other four do, which had
never been checked in a browser before. Both blocks matter: they have equal
specificity, so a theme that set only `:root` would apply its dark colours in
light mode and look like a broken toggle rather than a broken theme.

`index.html`'s heading does not use `--accent` and did not change — correct, not
a failure. It is listed so the next reader does not take it for one.

## Step 6 — the tracers against code this repository did not write

The suites run the tracers against fixtures this repository wrote, which prove
the contract and prove nothing about the heuristics: a resolver that silently
resolves nothing still emits a valid, well-shaped, empty-graph document.

| Tracer | Corpus | Files | Functions | Call edges | Entry points | Components |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trace_python.py` | CPython 3.11 standard library | 670 | 14,720 | 16,896 | 34 | — |
| `trace_typescript.mjs` | PrimeVue 5.0.1 | 820 | 5,817 | 3,384 | 0 | **423** |
| `trace_typescript.mjs` | TypeScript 5.6.3 compiler | 7 | 20,707 | **79,278** | 1 | 7 |
| `trace_rust.py` | serde_json 1.0.133 and 9 dependencies | 301 | 5,634 | 9,341 | 25 | — |
| `trace_java.py` | Gson, Commons Lang 3, picocli, JUnit console | 367 | 6,620 | 6,457 | 2 | — |
| `trace_c_family.py` | `/usr/include` | 4,145 | 12,765 | 6,387 | 0 | — |

`componentsFound` is the number the checklist says to sanity-check against what
the app has: **423 components against PrimeVue's 416 `.vue` files**, the excess
being the seven components declared outside a single-file component.

The two zeroes were checked rather than accepted:

- **PrimeVue finds 0 entry points**, correct for a component library: there is no
  `main`, no `index.html` and no app root anywhere in the package. A library has
  no entry point, and inventing one would be worse than reporting none.
- **C family finds 0 entry points in `/usr/include`**, correct for a header tree.
  Four files match `int main(`: three are inside Javadoc-style comment blocks in
  C++ headers (`basic_ios.h`, `bitset`, `tr2/dynamic_bitset`) and the fourth is
  inside a `#define` continuation in `cursesapp.h`. The tracer masks comments and
  preprocessor lines, so it is right to see none.
- **Java found 0 entry points across Gson and Commons Lang alone** — both are
  libraries. Adding picocli and JUnit's console launcher took it to exactly 2,
  which is the number of real `main` methods in the corpus.

The last part of step 6 — build a whole map from tracer output rather than by
re-reading — was run with `scripts/build-map.py` against PrimeVue. It completes:
**5,817 functions catalogued, 0 duplicated ids**, 0 flows (there is no entry
point to trace from), and the map's `functionsCatalogued` equals the tracer's
`functionsFound` exactly, which is what "used the output" means.

## What this pass found

### The TypeScript tracer pointed every class one line above itself

`trace_typescript.mjs` catalogues a class with the line number of its regex
match, and the regex opens with `(?:^|[^\w$.])` — a group that consumes the
character *before* the declaration whenever there is one. That character is
almost always the newline ending the line above, so the match index sat on the
previous line.

Every consumer of a class's line was wrong by exactly one:

- **Angular** components, directives, pipes, services and modules — all of them
  go through `angularComponents`, which reads `cls.line`.
- **React class components** — the `extends Component` branch reads the same field.
- **Entry points** mounted at an app root, which carry `component.line` onward.

Measured on the fixtures: `DashboardComponent` is declared on line 8 of
`dashboard.component.ts` and was recorded at 7; `ReportService` on line 4,
recorded at 3; `SummaryComponent` on line 7, recorded at 6. A class starting at
byte 0 of its file was the only case that came out right, because there is no
preceding character for the group to eat.

**Why it matters more than a line number usually does.** A `file:line` is the
whole product: the report, the QA walkthrough and the diagram all exist so a
reader can go and look at the same line the tool looked at. An id also carries
the line when two definitions in a file share a name, so a wrong line propagates
into `_l<line>` and changes the id a call graph refers to a function by.

**Fixed in this pass**, in the commit that carries this file. The leading group
matched `^` exactly when the match starts with a word character and consumed
nothing; otherwise it ate one character. `declStart` steps over that one
character before the line number is taken, which is the whole fix.

Before and after, over the same corpora:

| Corpus | Catalogued entries | Ids changed by the fix | Components moved onto their declaration line |
|---|---|---|---|
| PrimeVue 5.0.1 | 5,817 | 11 | 1 of 422 |
| This repository (TypeScript only) | 98 | 0 | 3 of 8 |

PrimeVue's eleven are the classes in `inputcolor/index.mjs` and
`passthrough/index.mjs`. Two pairs among them are worth reading, because they
show the id rule from v1.2.0 doing its job: `multiplymatrices_l61` and
`multiplymatrices_l62` were only distinguishable *because* of the bug — the class
was being recorded one line above the function it shares a name with. With both
on line 62 where they belong, the same-line suffix takes over and they become
`multiplymatrices_l62_1` and `multiplymatrices_l62_2`. The same happens to
`parsecolor` and to `usePassThrough`.

**Test added.** `test_typescript_tracer_points_a_component_at_the_line_it_is_declared_on`
reads the fixture app's own source and asserts each non-SFC component's recorded
line names it. It fails on the pre-fix tracer with
`assert 'DashboardComponent' in '})'` and passes after. Nothing in either suite
had ever compared a recorded line against the file it points into; that is the
gap that let this ship in 1.1.0 and 1.2.0.

`.vue` and `.svelte` components are excluded from that test and are **not** a
bug: a single-file component has no declaration to point at. The file is the
component, and line 1 is the honest answer.

### Two documentation rules this repository breaks

Found by the violations run and confirmed by reading. **Both are fixed in the
commit that carries this file** — neither blocked a release, but both are a
reader following the documentation and not getting what it describes.

- **RULES-01 (high)** — `_SHARED_FILES` in `src/code_flow_skill/cli.py` installs
  thirteen files into `.code-flow/`. README's manual-install recipe copies four.
  Missing are `bundle.template.html`, `theme.css` and the whole `tracers/`
  directory — so a reader who installs by hand has no `--tracer`, which the same
  README documents two sections later as available to every tool. The recipe now
  copies all thirteen: the five scaffolds, `theme.css`, and `tracers/`.
- **RULES-02 (medium)** — the sentence opening "Before publishing" names four
  scaffolds where five ship; `qa.template.html` was missing from it, while the
  numbered steps below it and the list closing the same section both name all
  five. Added.

### One quality finding dropped on reading

`firstExisting` in `trace_typescript.mjs:1315` tripped the `pass-through`
detector: one outbound call, under five lines, same arity as its callee. Reading
it settles that it is not one — `candidates(base).find((c) => fileSet.has(c)) || null`
builds a list, filters it with a predicate and falls back to null, which is three
pieces of work rather than a hand-off. Dropped, and the coverage banner says so.

## Step 4 — the skills on a real host

**Performed by the maintainer on the Red Sea Project**, one of their own
repositories, and reported in conversation on 2026-09-24. It could not be done
from here: there is no Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Codex or Antigravity host
in this environment to install into and watch discover a skill. Claude did not
observe the run, so this section records that it happened rather than what it
showed. The host it was run on, and whether the explicit-invocation sub-step —
that a host presents these skills as invoked-by-name only, which is what every
`No` row in the README's guarantee table claims — was looked at, are not recorded
here.

It covers **four** skills as of 1.3.0 (`code-flow-map`, `code-flow-quality`,
`code-flow-qa`, `code-flow-violations`). It holds for this branch as well as for
`master`: the checklist says a change to a skill's name or frontmatter re-opens
the step, and nothing here touches one. The diff changes the TypeScript tracer,
one test, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and this file — no `SKILL.md`, no
`agents/openai.yaml`, no command template under `templates/claude/`,
`templates/gemini/` or `templates/copilot/`, and neither installer.

With it, nothing in the checklist is outstanding.
